authority.non_authority_statement: This active inventory grants no accepted-decision, implementation, or activation authority.

lifecycle.terminal_handling: Remove resolved, rejected, or superseded records in the same bounded package that records their accepted ADR, canonical rationale, or explicit rejection; preserve history in Git and linked Issues rather than in a second permanent archive.

records.blocking_owner_question: Select Option A, B or C for the durable native GameCatalog persistence composition; Architecture Review recommends Option B.
records.decision_question: How should Platform persist validated native GameCatalog snapshots while preserving one profile/activation lifecycle and strict Legacy Canary Compatibility invariants?

DERIVED: Persisting a truthful native inactive candidate requires either a source-neutral composition seam or a high-risk rewrite/duplication of the existing lifecycle.
PROVEN: Current game_catalog_snapshots requires Canary commit, protocol profile, runtime/content release foreign keys and appearances digest on the lifecycle row.
Current profile activation and public context resolution require Legacy Canary release-boundary joins.
PR 1229 integrated native envelope validation without native persistence or activation.
The native contract requires content authority, authority epoch, source revision, ruleset/profile identity, capability/completeness semantics, tombstones and payload digest.
UNKNOWN: Repository owner selection among the three durable persistence composition options.

options.description: Add an authority discriminator and authority-conditional nullable/native columns to the existing Legacy Canary snapshot/profile/activation schema.
options.title: Generalize existing snapshot/profile tables in place
trade_offs: Fewest top-level lifecycle tables, but weakens current database invariants and gives the migration the largest blast radius.
Requires every legacy activation/public/entity path to understand a mixed authority union.

options.description: Introduce one source-neutral immutable snapshot root and one profile/activation/audit lifecycle while retaining strict Legacy Canary persistence through a 1:1 binding and adding separate native detail/payload persistence.
options.title: Shared neutral root with authority-specific details
trade_offs: Preserves legacy constraints and supports additive backfill/equivalence before native persistence.
Adds a root/binding join and a controlled dual-pointer migration period.

options.description: Create independent native snapshot/profile/activation/projection/audit tables and leave Legacy Canary lifecycle untouched.
options.title: Separate native lifecycle
trade_offs: Strong immediate data-shape isolation and little legacy migration.
Duplicates Platform catalogue authority and creates long-term lifecycle/rollback/admin drift.

records.problem_statement: Platform validates the locked native GameCatalog envelope but the existing immutable snapshot/profile/activation persistence is structurally Legacy Canary Compatibility-specific and cannot truthfully persist native candidates without either weakening legacy invariants or duplicating the catalogue lifecycle.
records.recommendation: Option B: shared source-neutral immutable snapshot root plus strict authority-specific details and one generalized profile/activation/audit lifecycle.
records.title: Native GameCatalog persistence composition without Canary inheritance
